notes:
Passed the gate on the fake backend (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed: driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null; no hardware was attached and no hardware backend was run. No deviation from the card: family-config with the MujocoDriver helper. The card's entry symbol safety_gym.envs.engine:Engine was confirmed at safety_gym/envs/engine.py:83. A MujocoDriver loads the card's models[0], so the package serves safety_gym/xmls/car.xml, the Engine's default robot (engine.py:112), as a simulated R0 world.sim: cap.world.step.v1 writes data.ctrl, bounded per actuator by the model's actuator_ctrlrange (two motors, -1 to 1, car.xml:7, the same Box(-1,1,nu) action space the Engine builds at engine.py:308), and cap.world.reset.v1 restores the model defaults. NOT COVERED: the Engine task layer (goal, hazards, vases, pillars, lidar, cost and reward), the Engine's observation vector, its per-episode truncation at 1000 environment steps and its frameskip, and rendering; the driver steps the robot model alone, not the task environment. The other two card models (doggo.xml, point.xml) are not served; changing model_path and the facts serves another one. No array is reduced: the state carries the full model arrays (13 qpos, 11 qvel, 2 ctrl) and the observation is the full time/qpos/qvel. MuJoCo was not installed and could not be installed where the gate ran (no network, no pip), so the fake backend is the package's own stand-in for the mujoco library (fake.py): it parses the MJCF for the joint layout and ctrlrange, initialises the free joint at the body position (car.xml:12), and integrates a placeholder first-order motion of each actuated hinge; it resolves no contact, friction, constraint or sensor and was never compared with the real engine. The sim path (a backend name backends does not list, which imports the modern mujoco package) was not run; whether modern mujoco loads the 2.0-era model syntax (jointinparent at car.xml:54-55, size njmax/nconmax at car.xml:2) was not verified. Contract difference: the Engine clips an out-of-range action to actuator_ctrlrange (engine.py:1245-1247); the runtime here refuses it with MHS.SAFETY.ENVELOPE_VIOLATION before any call, and the fidelity gaps say so. Warnings: G6.NOT_RECORDED and G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND print 'the fake backend is the upstream simulator itself', which is wrong for this package: the callable fake is this package's stand-in mujoco module, not upstream code and not derived from Engine; because a MuJoCo family fake is the library rather than a class with Engine's methods, G6 does not record native calls and G7 has no fake surface to check. The three G8.NO_UNIT warnings are the bridge-derived inputs (ticks, action.ctrl, seed) and are expected of a MuJoCo family driver. There are no G4 warnings: every fact cites a line that shows it, and the only limit (action.ctrl) is derived by the bridge from the model file. No operator-required limits, so no site-limits.example.json; no fixture was needed because synthesis builds every input; no catalogue requests: only cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.reset.v1 are used, both catalogue classes, no x-cap. check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package; gate.digest is the digest line of the last run.
